newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - RJB on target for objectives.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - RJB on target for objectives.

text.p: RJB Mining is "still on target to achieve (its) prospectus objectives," chief executive Richard Budge told Reuters in an interview.
He said demand was "holding up pretty well," with incursions into the market by gas suppliers "no more than we forecast."
Budge said total energy demand in the UK was up five percent in the first six months of 1996, well above the 1.5 percent rise forecast and the 2.6 percent increase seen a year ago.
RJB turned in pretax profits of 86.06 million stg for the six months to end-June, little changed from 85.76 million a year ago, as sales slipped to 697.2 million from 739.6 million stg.
It paid out a dividend of eight pence, up from 5.5 pence previously.
"There's lots of good stuff in here," Budge said.
He said the company aimed to consolidate its UK business, aiming to keep sales steady.
"We are...consolidating the UK business, that is where the long-term future lies," Budge said.

"The strategy is to maintain current sales into the next century," he added. He said the company's mine at Asfordby was in the first phase of a new mine plan to see if operations were viable and "early indications are encouraging."
At Thorne, near Doncaster in northern England, another colliery was waiting to reopen while the company said with its half year results it was applying to open a mine at Witham.
"We are ensuring the long-term profile for the company," Budge said.
The new Witham mine would take 10-15 years to come into production with investment of around 300 million stg.
It would employ 300-500 people, depending on production levels, Budge said, with some of the posts possible transfers from Selby, where resources are expected to be exhausted.
Budge said first results from CIM, the Australian company in which it has a strategic stake, were "very promising. It is going well."
He said CIM was "an exploratory investment at the moment," but added that he would not rule out further expansions by RJB in the future.
